8

Strings

Text manipulation with Ika domain

Ika: The Odù of Language

In Yoruba tradition, ika is associated with speech and communication. In Ifá-Lang, the Ika domain handles all string manipulation.

Creating Strings

String Basics 
ayanmo greeting = "Hello, Ifá!";
ayanmo empty = "";
ayanmo multiline = "Line 1\nLine 2\nLine 3";

// String concatenation
ayanmo first = "Ifá";
ayanmo last = "Lang";
ayanmo full = first + " " + last;
let greeting = "Hello, Ifá!";
let empty = "";
let multiline = "Line 1\nLine 2\nLine 3";

// String concatenation
let first = "Ifá";
let last = "Lang";
let full = first + " " + last;

String Length

Length 
ayanmo text = "Ifá-Lang";
Irosu.fo(Ika.gun(text));  // 8 (length)

// Empty string
Irosu.fo(Ika.gun(""));    // 0

Case Manipulation

Case Methods 
ayanmo word = "Ifá-Lang";

Ika.nla(word);       // uppercase → "IFÁ-LANG"
Ika.kekere(word);    // lowercase → "ifá-lang"

Substring and Trimming

Substring & Trim 
ayanmo phrase = "  Hello, Ifá-Lang!  ";

// Extract substring (start, length)
Ika.ge_lara(phrase, 8, 4);  // "Ifá" (from index 8, 4 chars)

// Trim whitespace
Ika.ge(phrase);             // "Hello, Ifá-Lang!"

Checking Content

Contains & Starts/Ends With 
ayanmo text = "Hello, Ifá-Lang!";

Ika.ni(text, "Ifá");          // contains → otito (true)
Ika.ni(text, "Rust");         // contains → iro (false)

Ika.bẹrẹ(text, "Hello");      // starts with → otito
Ika.parí(text, "!");          // ends with → otito

Splitting and Joining

Split & Join 
ayanmo csv = "apple,banana,cherry";
ayanmo parts = Ika.pín(csv, ",");  // ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]

ayanmo joined = Ika.dapọ(parts, ", ");  // "apple, banana, cherry"

Finding and Replacing

Find & Replace 
ayanmo sentence = "Ifá-Lang is amazing";

// Find index of substring
Ika.wa(sentence, "Lang");     // find → 4 (index of match)

// Replace all occurrences
Ika.rọpo(sentence, "amazing", "powerful");  // "Ifá-Lang is powerful"

Character Access

Character at Index 
ayanmo name = "Ifá";

Ika.kọ(name, 0);    // char at index 0 → "I"
Ika.kọ(name, 1);    // char at index 1 → "f"
Ika.kọ(name, 2);    // char at index 2 → "á"
Unicode Aware

Ika methods work with Unicode characters, not bytes. Yoruba characters with diacritics (ẹ, ọ, ṣ, etc.) are treated as single characters.

What You Learned

  • String basics: creation, concatenation
  • Ika.gun() for length
  • Ika.nla/kekere for case
  • Ika.ge_lara/ge for substring & trim
  • Ika.ni/bẹrẹ/parí for content checks
  • Ika.pín/dapọ for split & join
  • Ika.wa/rọpo for find & replace
  • Ika.kọ for character access
